suppress.notes: beer.thierry:paypal is this project's own integration submodule (centsible-integrations:paypal), not the public PayPal SDK. Version 0.3.0 happens to collide with an old paypal/paypal-* npm package CPE. The CVEs are from 2013 against a Node.js library we don't ship.

com.google.devtools.ksp:symbol-processing-api is the Kotlin Symbol Processing API, not the Processing IDE/language (processing.org). CVE-2018-1000840 is an XXE in the Processing IDE, which is unrelated to KSP.
spring-boot-sql is incorrectly matched against the "www-sql" CPE (a different, unrelated project). The legitimate spring-boot CPE matches still apply.
spring-boot-web-server is incorrectly matched against a generic "web_project:web" CPE. The legitimate spring-boot CPE matches still apply.
hibernate-validator is incorrectly matched against a generic "validator:validator" CPE for an unrelated project. The legitimate hibernate / redhat hibernate_validator matches still apply.

CVE-2026-0994 is a recursion-depth bypass in google.protobuf.json_format.ParseDict() in the Python protobuf implementation. The fixed version (6.33.x) is a Python release; the Java implementation does not contain ParseDict and is not affected. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7gcm-g887-7qv7.

CVE-2025-1686 is a server-side template injection in Pebble that requires an attacker to control template source. centsible-export only loads templates from the classpath (PebbleConfig uses ClasspathLoader; templates are packaged at build time and never sourced from user input), so the vulnerability is not reachable.
